headline: Australia’s Unemployment Rate Rises to 4.9%
deck: Most of the seasonally adjusted employment decline came from part-time work, while participation fell to 66.6%.
body: Australia’s seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 4.9% in October, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said, its highest level since October 2021 [E4]. ABC reported that the displayed September rate was 4.7%, also on a seasonally adjusted basis [E7].

Seasonally adjusted employment fell by 43,500 people to 14,738,600. The decline was concentrated in part-time employment, down 40,600, while full-time employment fell by 2,900 [E1]. ABC reported that the number of officially unemployed people rose by 17,800 [E8]. These are counts of people in employment, separate from the unemployment rate and from measures of hours worked.
Youth unemployment rose to 11.3% from 11.1% in September [E5]. The employment-to-population ratio fell 0.3 percentage points to 63.3%, while participation fell 0.2 percentage points to 66.6% [E6].

For the October release, the ABS adjusted the weighting of about 1,390 Victorian respondents, about 2.7% of the sample, to keep the survey representative [E2]. The bureau advises caution over short-term changes and says its trend series is the better guide to underlying labour-market behaviour [E3]. It also notes that the survey is subject to sampling and non-sampling error; its published confidence intervals for seasonally adjusted movements are based on a typical month [E9][E10].

evidence_box.fragment: Australia's unemployment rate surged to 4.9 per cent in October, up from 4.7 per cent in September in seasonally adjusted terms. The surprisingly large jump in unemployment comes after the Reserve Bank lifted interest rates for the fifth time this year. But that interest rate hike, earlier this month, had no bearing on the employment data because the increase in unemployment occurred well before that rate hike.
